title: Map-first signatures: First Stand field proof

cards.title: Posts establish the doctrine
cards.trigger: The always-on Hold Mid tactic assigns every bot an exact player-authored post and facing.
cards.tactic: The team occupies a readable formation while Hold combat may leave a post briefly to answer threats.
cards.counterplay: Attack a weak edge, split the formation's attention, or pressure it outside the useful range of its posts.
cards.fallback: When contact ends, ordinary positioning Instructions pull survivors back toward their authored ground.
cards.watch: Watch a holder rotate and engage instead of dying passively to an enemy approaching from the side.

cards.title: Smart skills are opportunities
cards.trigger: A threatened lane, damaged ally, vulnerable enemy, or other class-specific opportunity appears around mid.
cards.tactic: Unmarked skills use conservative Smart presets; the Lantern's authored point remains explicit map guidance.
cards.counterplay: Spread out, preserve distance, or wait out deployments so the preset's usefulness test is not satisfied.
cards.fallback: A declined skill never consumes the bot's turn; the current movement or combat behavior continues.
cards.watch: Use selected-bot action reasons to distinguish fired signatures from named, nonempty opportunity declines.

cards.title: Selected geometry stays literal
cards.trigger: Ratchet is near its marked Flare point and the contextual anti-smoke opportunity is legal.
cards.tactic: The mark says where Survey Flare may be used; the server catalog, editor, materializer, and runtime share that geometry contract.
cards.counterplay: Avoid committing smoke near the mark or force Ratchet away before the opportunity appears.
cards.fallback: Without hostile smoke, Ratchet keeps holding and fighting rather than wasting the cast.
cards.watch: The explicit point should remain visible and editable per bot, independently of every other Lantern.

cards.title: One combat continuation
cards.trigger: An enemy enters a holder's combat neighborhood from any facing.
cards.tactic: Hold, signature use, and ordinary fighting are branches of the same generated Instruction priority.
cards.counterplay: Bait a holder away, then change angle before it settles back onto its post.
cards.fallback: Losing sight ends that combat episode; the bot resumes its post instead of inventing a parallel chase state.
cards.watch: Look for rotation, a bounded chase off-post, and a clean return when the target is no longer nearby.

cards.title: Custody belongs to the Core
cards.trigger: Any bot takes a Core while its phase's pickup and delivery policy is active.
cards.tactic: That policy snapshots onto the Core for this team, surviving drops, handoffs, and later phase changes.
cards.counterplay: Separate the carrier from its original group, force a drop, or kill it before the team can bank.
cards.fallback: Carrier and attached escorts defend themselves but do not abandon custody for ordinary recovery behavior.
cards.watch: Follow the Core identity across possession changes; the policy is team-local and the former carrier can become an escort.

cards.title: One priority system
cards.trigger: Positioning, combat, recovery, custody, and signature opportunities compete during the same live tactic.
cards.tactic: Tactics compile to one ordered Instruction tree; signatures add contextual actions rather than a parallel scheduler.
cards.counterplay: Create competing pressure that exposes the authored priority choices while a useful signature is nearly ready.
cards.fallback: Every generated signature branch has an ordinary move, hold, fight, or custody continuation beneath it.
cards.watch: Scrub action reasons: a bot should not wait merely because its preferred signature is unavailable.
